title: P6a1: review-finding telemetry on every review — the review run row and the review task result carry verdict, findings_count, findings_by_severity, reviewer_role, checklist_used, reviewed_sha, packet_version and review_pass_index; a read-time helper derives the same fields for historical reviews from their stored comments
spec:
Phase I P6 (brief, section P6, inlined: do this only with review telemetry available; never remove reviews to reduce tokens; measure whether reduced context affects review findings; security-path requirements stay deterministic). Base goal/T-0489 (cut from goal/T-0445 at 4149f67). Work only in your own worktree and commit only on your own branch. Scout facts (T-0490): reviews are created by daemon._open_reviews (daemon.py:831-868) with reviewed_sha inherited and complexity bumped to SECURITY_CHECKLIST_COMPLEXITY (7) for security reviews; the review result is stored by bus.post_result as fit_result({"summary": ..., **result}) where result has verdict and comments [{path, line, issue, severity}] (spawn.py:730-753, 624-630); the review run row is logged by spawn.run_claude with role review, tier, usd, tokens and packet_meta (spawn.py:409-439; packet_meta carries the P1b packet version hash); the security section of review_packet fires on security globs, the semantic regex, complexity >= 7 or review_reason in security_paths, diff_unavailable, security_paths_empty (spawn.py:412-471); the adversarial-review skill contract returns only verdict and comments.
1. orchestrator/attribution.py: review_facts(review_task) -> dict {verdict, findings_count, findings_by_severity: {high, med, low, other} (severity normalised: high/critical -> high; med/medium -> med; low/info/nit -> low; else other), reviewer_role: constraints.reviewer_role or "general", checklist_used: bool (pipeline.review_reason names a security reason or complexity >= 7), reviewed_sha: constraints.reviewed_sha or pipeline.reviewed_sha, packet_version: result.packet_version or the review run row's packet_meta.version when present else None, review_pass_index: 1-based position of this review among the reviews of the same inputs[0] ordered by created_at (or id), reviews_expected: the reviewed task's pipeline.reviews_expected}. Works for every historical review task (fields None when absent, never raises).
2. spawn.run_worker for role review: after the result is extracted, compute review_facts from the posted result and stamp them on the review task (bus.update(review_id, review_facts=...)) and add the same keys to the run row via bus.log_run kwargs (findings_count, findings_by_severity, reviewer_role, checklist_used, reviewed_sha, packet_version, review_pass_index); the result dict posted also gets packet_version = the packet_meta version used for the prompt.
3. Tests tests/test_attribution.py: test_review_facts_normalises_severities_and_counts, test_review_facts_handles_missing_fields_on_old_reviews, test_review_facts_pass_index_orders_sibling_reviews; tests/test_spawn.py: test_review_run_row_and_task_carry_review_facts (mocked claude run returning a verdict with three comments; row and task carry the facts, packet_version equals the packet header hash). Existing tests green; full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exit 0; commit with the task id including every named test; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: every new review run row and review task carry verdict, findings_count, findings_by_severity, reviewer_role, checklist_used, reviewed_sha, packet_version and review_pass_index; historical reviews yield the same fields via attribution.review_facts
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree; the commit is on this task's own branch
